newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil eyes Barents Sea Snoehvit gas field.
newsitem.headline: Statoil eyes Barents Sea Snoehvit gas field.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) is pursuing plans to exploit oil and gas reserves in the Snoehvit prospect in the Barents Sea and other fields on the Tromsoe Patch off northern Norway, the company's Status Weekly newsletter said on Thursday.
The company has drawn a team from several business areas to produce possible development plans for Snoehvit over the next 18 to 24 months.
The field is estimated to hold about 150 billion cubic metres of recoverable gas.
Statoil will also work on a sales solution for liquefied natural gas (LNG) from the fields, it said.
"Finding a market for the gas is crucial to a Snoehvit development," said Snorre Jensen, head of the development team.
"...We see opportunities in the Middle East and the U.S. East Coast. The primary focus is on markets that do not compete with piped Norwegian gas."

The development could extend over four to five years at a probable cost of more than 15 billion crowns. Gas would be produced from subsea wells with new multiphase flow technology allowing the hydrocarbon streams to be piped to land for processing and liquefaction before export by ship.
Multilateral, or branched, wells could permit profitable recovery from the thin oil zones in Snoehvit, Statoil said.

"Technology already adopted for the Sleipner West field in the North Sea to remove carbon dioxide (CO2) from produced gas and inject it into an underground structure is also under consideration," it said.
Statoil will inject about one million tonnes per year of CO2 around 1,000 metres below the seabed at Sleipner West, the first offshore project to use this injection method.
